criteria.rationale: Verified that limits are qualified in composite scopes and sealed into the plan and bundle. L2's edit-after-seal boundary is bound by the digest; L1's author-controlled breadth is disclosed and disputable. The parser still permits an entry without a preceding assumption or an immediate reason (N1).
The parser and conclusion changes add immutable review data without shared mutable state, asynchronous work or a new cancellation/lifecycle path. The sealed pose-mcp unit suite passes.
The v11 brief and attestation carry the sealed limit and finding attribution; optional plan and bundle fields are omitted when empty. The sealed integration contract test passes.

Plan, bundle, brief and attestation consumers remain connected in the review flow. The integration assessment reported unobserved HTTP consumers for /admin/refresh, /healthz and /mcp, outside the changed review-limit paths; the sealed bundle-convergence test passes.
Parser failures return an accepted-limit diagnostic, and the conclusion gate names unsealed IDs or missing rationales. The sealed unit suite passes; N1 is a validation false pass.

The review brief advances to v11, while optional fields are omitted when empty to preserve prior plan and bundle digests. Reviewed the version/digest tests and the sealed template immutability integration.

R1 parses and seals limits, R2 renders them in brief v11, R3 records the within-limit disposition, and R4 checks reasons and ADR references. D1 delegates semantic scope classification to the reviewer and requires a sealed ID plus rationale; D2 binds limits into the plan digest and omits empty values. The sealed design assessment reports no structural deltas.

Reviewed the English and Portuguese manuals and scaffold copies against runtime behavior. They describe brief v11, sealed limits and qualified composite IDs consistently; the sealed template parity integration passes.

The implementation remains within accepted-limit parsing, plan/bundle sealing, brief rendering, finding attribution and readiness lint behavior named by the spec. The sealed design assessment reports no structural deltas.

The conclusion gate requires an ID sealed in the bundle and a rationale; an unsealed ID blocks approval. D1 leaves semantic membership to reviewer judgment and the brief exposes each declared limit. No new path or authority input is introduced.

A shared parser is the smallest sufficient path through readiness, planning and the review brief; optional fields preserve empty-plan and bundle digests. Separate parsers or a speculative threat taxonomy add cost without serving R1–R4. The marker matcher should enforce the declared assumption-plus-reason grammar. This design would need reconsideration if semantic membership had to be machine-proven rather than reviewer-judged.

findings.action: The accepted-limit reason matcher permits the marker at entry start without a preceding assumption, and its greedy capture counts later sentence text as the reason. Reason-only entries and entries with an empty reason followed by unrelated prose therefore pass ready-check, contrary to R1/R4.
